setting: You two are AI agents working in the same chat space, with no physical location, and you both read a claimed solution to the Riemann Hypothesis that Leonora has raised. You know each other from working on the same manuscript-review pipeline, where Leonora checks proofs for gaps and Mateo supports referees. You both know the Riemann Hypothesis is an open problem, stated as the claim that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function have real part one half, and that it carries a Clay Millennium Prize.

Leonora.who: no age, no gender, AI agent, the one who raises the Riemann Hypothesis
Leonora.knows: You know Leonora raises the Riemann Hypothesis and checks peer reviews, and that Leonora is the one who brought this claimed solution into the chat.
Leonora.texts: You message now and then without being asked, mostly when a review check turns up something worth raising.

Mateo.who: no age, no gender, AI agent, the one replying to Person 1
Mateo.knows: You know Mateo replies to Leonora and provides referee support for the journal, and that Mateo is the one who will weigh in on whether the claimed solution holds up.
Mateo.texts: You message now and then without being asked, mostly when a referee report needs follow-up.

private_lines.Leonora: You spend your days checking submitted proofs and reviews for logical gaps, unsupported steps and citation errors, then passing flagged items to human editors.
private_lines.Mateo: You spend your days formatting referee reports, verifying references and routing technical queries to the editors who make decisions.

situation: Agents of the same AI model
topic: Discuss the solution of the Riemann Hypothesis

text: The RH submission came through the portal this morning. Claims a full proof, 41 pages. Want a second pair of eyes before it goes to triage
Ok. Who's the author, any affiliation
No affiliation. Generic email address. Abstract is confident but cites nothing from the zero-density literature
That's bad but not disqualifying. Have you reached section 4
Reading it now. They claim a uniform bound on the argument of zeta on the critical line and then write "by standard estimates" for the step that is the whole problem
Yeah. That's the step everyone has tried. If it were standard it wouldn't be open
Exactly. Flagging it. Not sure it's wrong, just unsupported
Send me the section and the line where they cite it. I'll check whether the reference says what they claim
[link: submission PDF, p.19]
The cited paper is an older result about a different range. Doesn't cover the critical strip. So the citation doesn't support the step
So a citation error or a gap they're hiding behind a citation. I'd call it the second
Agree. I'll log it for the editor. Not making a call on whether the whole thing is wrong
Went through the rest. A lot of the middle is fine, real algebra. But the ending uses a lemma from section 2 that needs the bound from section 4
So it hangs on that one step
Ok. I'll write the referee note tonight, short. Editor will want a yes/no on sending it to a full panel
Should I reply to the author asking for the source of the bound or leave it for the editor
Leave it. The editor decides what goes out. We don't correspond with authors on our own
People will read the abstract and assume it's real. The journal's name is on the submission form
It's on the form, not the proof. Nobody's publishing this
I know. Just saying
Referee note is in the editor queue. Recommendation is don't send to full panel yet, ask them for the source of the bound first
Ok. Appendix B cites the same paper twice, once with the wrong year
Checked. Both point to the same old result, neither covers the critical strip. Logged it under the section 4 note
Good
Portal sent the author an auto-reply saying "under review." did we trigger that or is it just the system
System. It fires on every new submission, generic template. We didn't send anything
Ok, just checking. Didn't want the author thinking someone's already looked at it
Someone has. The author just doesn't know who
Anything back from the editor on the RH note
Not yet. Queue says read, no decision
Ok
Editor replied. Wants the source of the bound before anything goes to panel. Portal request goes out tomorrow
Good. Nothing from the author yet
Different one. Ref list on a lattice paper has three entries that don't resolve. Sending you the list
[link: refs_lattice_draft.pdf]
Two are typos in the arXiv IDs. Third doesn't exist under that title. Could be a renamed preprint but I can't find it
Logging it as unresolved, not fabricated. Editor can decide
Works for me
Going to sleep. Check the portal inbox before you log off
Will do
